units.translation: l. αἵματος Οὐρα〈νίοιο〉: Acusilaus in the third book (2 fg 4 J.) says that from the castration of Uranus drops, that is, drops, happened to fall upon the earth, from which the Phaeacians were born; but others say the Giants. And Alcaeus (fg 206 Lobel = 116 B. III 185) says the Phaeacians have their origin from the drops of Uranus, while Homer (ε 35. η 56 sqq.) says the Phaeacians are kin to the gods because of their descent from Poseidon.
993-94. τοὺς Ἀργὼ πολέεσσιν: the Argonauts, after suffering many hardships, were carried down from the Sicilian sea.
1000. 〈Αἱμονίη:〉 Thessaly. Lᶢ

1002-03 a. Κόλχων, οἱ Πόντοιο: of the Colchians, those who were with Absyrtus settled in the Brygean islands, which are part of Illyria, while those who came out through the Cyanean rocks settled Corcyra. For of the Colchians pursuing the chiefs, since they did not make the same voyage, some made their voyage through the Ister, as has been said before (IV 303 sqq.),

whom Absyrtus commanded, entering through the lower parts into the aforementioned river, and they overtook the heroes around the so-called Brygean islands; but the Colchians who made their exit through the Cyanean rocks arrived at the island of Corcyra, where the Argonauts happened to be.
b. μαστῆρες: seekers. Lᶢ (P)
1004. ἔξαιτον: chosen, special. Lᶢ (P)
1005 a. 〈ἵεντ’:〉 they were eager. Gᶢ
b. ἀπροφάτως: without pretext, unhesitatingly. Lᶢ (P)
1006. 〈ἀτροπίῃσιν:〉 evil ways, unalterably. Lᶢ
1015-17 a. εἴ νυ καὶ αὐτὴ ἀνθρώπων γενεῆς περὶ αὑτῆς ἡ Μήδεια· 〈. . .〉: you too are a human being, for whom erring comes easily. L

b. In the phrase "if indeed you too are of the race of humans," Medea strongly draws Arete to compassion, for both because we are of the same nature we ought to pity one another, and because we are quick to be swayed by emotions. P
1019. Ἠελίοιο: since he is the ancestor of Medea. Lᵐ (P)
1020. Hecate is an oath among the Colchians and sorceresses; for the goddess is the inventor of such things.
1024. 〈ἔτι μοι μίτρη μένει:〉 meaning: I am still a virgin. Lᶢ
1027. τελεσφόρον: the one who brings all things to fulfillment. Lᵐ (P)
1031-35. For the sake of your labors, O best of men, I am in great turmoil; for by my counsel you yoked the bulls and mowed down the earth-born men, and now you will carry off the fleece to Thessaly.
1043 a. 〈νέμεσίν τε θεῶν:〉 the nemesis that comes into the hands of the gods, that is, the object of divine wrath. Lᵐ
b. He says that the nemesis that occurs in supplications comes into the hands of the gods, because we supplicate as if standing before the gods; therefore we also respect those who supplicate. P
1045-46 a. 〈οὐ νηούς:〉 for I have no temple as a helper, nor tower, nor anyone else at all, but you are my entire safety. Lᵐ
